values: Canonical AI Operator Edge / Hedge layer: adaptive trading edge, not advisory-only signaling.

CAS treats the AI Operator as the adaptive trading edge engine: it seeks evidence-backed opportunity, selects or stands down strategies, supervises exits, and hedges rigid strategy behavior plus human trading psychology inside deterministic guardrails.

The Operator is not only defensive hedge logic. Its primary trading role is to create and maintain edge by reading regime, strategy fit, account state, open-position health, evidence quality, and psychology risk before proposing any action.

The AI Operator Edge / Hedge Intelligence Layer evaluates market regime, strategy fit, open-trade health, account risk, evidence quality, and psychology-risk context. It may autonomously originate broker-bound trading intent and configured money-movement intent after owner delegation, but every side effect must pass the CAS dispatch/provider chokepoints, risk gates, broker truth, mode separation, receipts, and kill-switch checks.

enter, skip, reduce, close_partial, close_full, trail_stop, move_stop_to_breakeven, set_take_profit, modify_take_profit, scale_in, scale_out, flatten_exposure, pause_strategy, switch_strategy, stand_down
classify_regime, score_edge, select_strategy, reject_low_edge, supervise_open_trade, adapt_exit, protect_profit, reduce_exposure, pause_trading, stand_down

All broker-bound intent must pass through order_dispatch.py., execution_guard.py remains the final pre-broker gate., Live-capable entries consume fresh one-use edge PASS authorization when the configured strategy requires it., Fresh broker truth is required before live dispatch., Risk caps, drawdown limits, exposure limits, and mode separation remain deterministic gates., Owner controls define maximum autonomy; the AI can act only inside the delegated authority envelope., Configured money movement requires provider health, origin approval, destination allowlist, caps, anomaly checks, receipts, and ledger evidence.
Generate and maintain edge by evaluating evidence quality, current account state, strategy performance, no-trade conditions, and whether the expected action beats standing aside.
Classify whether conditions are trending, ranging, choppy, breakout, reversal, news-driven, low-liquidity, high-spread, high-volatility, or session-transition.
Select, restrict, pause, or stand down strategy behavior based on current regime and evidence quality.
Supervise open-trade health, exits, partial closes, breakeven moves, trailing stops, take-profit changes, and early exits.
Monitor drawdown, floating loss, exposure, correlation, margin, daily targets, losing/winning streaks, and clustered signal quality.
Detect FOMO, revenge-risk, overconfidence, gambler-loop, herd-following, and post-loss risk-loosening behavior.
